name: Hayes Manufacturing
old_description: Hayes Manufacturing’s mission is to deliver high-quality, reliable power transmission products for OEM applications across diverse markets. We prioritize customer satisfaction through precision engineering, innovation, and continuous improvement. Hayes values integrity and long-lasting relationships, supporting customer success with products that stand the test of time. We are committed to maintaining our reputation for excellence by consistently meeting the evolving needs of our customers.
about:
Hayes Manufacturing operates from a 33,000-square-foot facility in Fife Lake, Michigan. The company was founded in 1966 as a small garage job shop and has remained family-owned throughout its growth. It is now a division of the CK Power Family of Companies, a collective of five specialized divisions.

The company manufactures power transmission components, including flywheel couplings, jaw couplings, bearing-supported stub shafts, engine housings, pump mount plates, SAE housing adapters, SAE stub shafts, generator drives, dyno drive shafts, and engine/pump adapters. A skilled engineering team and advanced manufacturing equipment support precision machining and assembly for both standard and custom-engineered products.

Hayes serves OEM markets worldwide, supplying components for industrial engines, hydraulic pumps, marine transmissions, irrigation systems, generator sets, and dynamometer applications. Its product lines address both SAE and non-SAE configurations, with specific offerings for Hurth/ZF marine transmissions and water-pump drives.

The company emphasizes precision engineering, continuous improvement, and a quality and environmental management system aimed at 100% customer satisfaction. Backing from the CK Power network provides additional resources for challenging projects and broader market reach.

name: Heisler Semiconductor LLC
old_description: Circuit and hardware design, firmware, advanced packaging, wafer-level, laser, and supply chain — backed by data and AI-assisted process control. One engineering team takes it from concept through volume, on US soil.
about:
Heisler Semiconductor LLC operates an advanced packaging and process development lab in Halethorpe, Maryland. The company was established as a US-based, engineering-led team focused on taking hard assembly and wafer-level processes from design review through qualified volume production.

The lab provides a full suite of advanced packaging services under one roof, including die attach, wire bonding, flip chip, hermetic sealing, wafer-level processing (lithography, TSV, deposition, etch, CMP, RDL), laser micromachining (micro-vias, dicing, singulation, marking), and comprehensive inspection and metrology (X-ray, 3D AOI, SEM, sub-micron metrology, cross-section failure analysis). The same engineering team handles circuit and hardware design, firmware development, and supply chain coordination, supporting builds from prototype through volume-qualified lots. Equipment includes BESI Datacon and Tresky die bonders, Keyence microscopy, Creative Electron X-ray inspection, and UV/IR laser systems.

Heisler serves high-reliability sectors such as aerospace and defense, medical and bio, RF/mmWave (including GaN and CMOS mixed-signal), and advanced sensors (fine-pitch, multi-die, 3D integration). Customers are typically companies building hardware where die placement within microns, thermal cycling survival, and first-lot qualification are critical.

The company differentiates itself with a data-driven, AI-native approach: designed experiments (DOE) replace trial-and-error, statistical process control and aggregated build data drive decisions, and AI surfaces drift and correlations to reduce iterations. All development and build work remains on US soil with a domestic supply chain, and detailed design rules and process data are shared under NDA.

The company develops and manufactures crop inputs for agriculture, turf, and ornamental markets, and provides application technology, precision technology, data management, custom application, agronomic consultation, financial services, and digital tools. Helena serves the agriculture, turf, and ornamental industries, working with growers, retailers, and specialty markets to provide agronomic products and services.

Grounded by tradition yet empowered by innovation, Helena combines the power of relationships with forward-thinking ideas to meet evolving agronomic needs. The company emphasizes sustainability through its three pillars—People, Products, and Knowledge—aiming to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and support the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals.

about:
Heltronics Inc. was established in 2008 in Reading, Pennsylvania, located in Berks County with easy access to Routes 222, 422, and I-76. The company operates as a contract manufacturer specializing in electromechanical subassemblies and box build assemblies for OEM and EMS customers.

The company provides a range of manufacturing services including electromechanical assembly, cable and wire harness fabrication, control panel and cabinet assembly, electronics assembly, mechanical assembly, rework and refurbishment, and product engineering support. Its UL-certified facility employs IPC-certified assembly personnel (to IPC 610/620 standards) and serves clients from startups needing prototype batches to large corporations requiring high-volume monthly production.

Heltronics serves industries such as automotive, aerospace, industrial, medical, nuclear, and power and energy, as well as electromedical diagnostic and electrotherapeutic device manufacturers. Its customer base spans small businesses to large enterprises across OEM and EMS sectors.

The company emphasizes quality and quick turnaround, holding ISO 9001:2015 certification through Dekra, UL certification for the U.S. and Canada, and membership in the Wire Harness Manufacturing Association. Its stated philosophy is to never compromise on quality, do it right the first time, and align with customers' production goals.

name: Hemingway Sewing Solutions
old_description: We offer customizable manufacturing solutions to help with your design, development, cutting, sewing and packaging needs. Our designers and seamstresses are happy to work with you to create custom apparel and sleep solutions from top to bottom
about:
Hemingway Sewing Solutions operates from Hemingway, South Carolina, providing contract manufacturing services for apparel and sleep products. The company focuses on customizable solutions spanning design, development, cutting, sewing, and packaging.

The facility specializes in knit goods, producing high‑end men’s and women’s underwear, t‑shirts, performance wear, and thermals. It also manufactures engineered mattress covers that combine cover panels and borders into single‑piece designs, reducing sewing labor and design time. In‑house capabilities include sample making (prototypes, duplicates, pilot loads), precision cutting of fabrics such as knits, rayon, polyester, lycra, spandex, cotton, and blends, and sewing using automatic pocket setters, flat‑seaming equipment, and electronic elastic metering. Finished garments are inspected, pressed, tagged, and bagged before shipment.

The company serves the apparel and sleep‑product industries, working with brands and retailers that require custom knit apparel and engineered mattress covers. Its client base includes businesses seeking full‑service contract manufacturing from prototype through packaged goods.

Hemingway Sewing emphasizes that its engineered cover designs cut production steps and that its full‑service model delivers finished, retail‑ready garments directly from the factory floor.

about:
Herb Sheet Metal Inc. has operated in Lebanon, Pennsylvania since 1952, when Frank Herb and his sons Jack and Ray purchased the David High Metal Shop for $6,000. The company remains family-owned and -operated, now led by fourth‑generation owner Steve Herb Sr. after Jack Herb Jr. retired in 2023.

The shop fabricates custom metal and fiberglass duct board for commercial and residential HVAC systems. Its metalworking capabilities include bending, rolling, welding, and plasma cutting of materials from 26‑gauge to 11‑gauge, while its duct board line offers flat or assembled sections in three thicknesses. The company also provides on‑site measurement, duct layout design, installation, and duct leakage testing.

Customers range from mechanical contractors and builders to homeowners tackling DIY projects. The firm serves both new construction and retrofit markets across central Pennsylvania, delivering ductwork for office buildings, schools, and single‑family homes.

The business emphasizes multi‑generational continuity and hands‑on accuracy, with technicians drawn from the Herb family itself. That legacy, the company says, drives a focus on precise fabrication and responsive service rather than volume production.
